facts.text: Don Giovanni premiered in Prague at the National Theatre (today’s Estates Theatre) on 29 October 1787.
facts.evidence: now called the Estates Theatre, on 29 October 1787

facts.text: It was meant to open on 14 October 1787 for a visiting archduchess, but wasn’t ready, so Le Nozze di Figaro was played instead.
facts.evidence: it was not ready in time and Le nozze di Figaro was substituted

facts.text: Prague commissioned it after Mozart’s successful visit there in early 1787.
facts.evidence: The opera was commissioned after the success of Mozart's trip to Prague in January and February 1787.

facts.text: The overture opens with a thundering D minor cadence and a mysterious passage, then turns into a light-hearted D major allegro.
facts.evidence: The overture begins with a thundering D minor cadence, followed by a short misterioso sequence which leads into a light-hearted D major allegro.

facts.text: The Catalogue Aria counts the Don’s conquests: 640 in Italy, 231 in Germany, 100 in France, 91 in Turkey, and in Spain, 1,003.
facts.evidence: his conquests include 640 women and girls in Italy, 231 in Germany, 100 in France, 91 in Turkey, but in Spain, 1,003

facts.text: Thanks to this aria, German and other languages call fold-out brochures a “Leporello list”.
facts.evidence: provided the name "Leporello list" for pamphlets

facts.text: “Là ci darem la mano” (“There we will entwine our hands”): alone with Zerlina, the Don immediately turns on the charm.
facts.evidence: Don Giovanni and Zerlina are soon alone and he immediately begins his seductive arts

facts.text: The “Champagne Aria”: the Don orders a party with every girl Leporello can find.
facts.evidence: tells Leporello to organise a party and invite every girl he can find

facts.text: Mozart added “Dalla sua pace” for the 1788 Vienna production, written for the tenor Francesco Morella.
facts.evidence: Don Ottavio's aria "Dalla sua pace" (K. 540a, composed on 24 April for the tenor Francesco Morella)

facts.text: Elvira’s “Mi tradì quell’alma ingrata” was also a Vienna addition, composed on 30 April 1788 for Caterina Cavalieri.
facts.evidence: composed on 30 April for the soprano Caterina Cavalieri

facts.text: In Prague and Vienna one singer played both Masetto and the Commendatore. The demons’ chorus gave him just a little time to change costume.
evidence: the same singer played both Masetto and the Commendatore roles in both the Prague and Vienna premieres
gives the singer time for a costume change before entering as Masetto for the sextet, though not much time

facts.sceneMatch: Questo è il fin|Questo e il fin|Ah, dov.è il perfido
facts.text: A memoirist claimed the final ensemble was heard only at the first Prague performance, then never again during the original run. Today it is almost always performed.
evidence: the final ensemble was only presented at the first performance in Prague, then never heard again during the original run
the final ensemble is almost invariably performed in full today

facts.text: Kierkegaard argued that “among all classic works Don Giovanni stands highest.” Gounod called it “a work without blemish, of uninterrupted perfection”.
evidence: among all classic works Don Giovanni stands highest.
a work without blemish, of uninterrupted perfection
